title: Formal Assumption Harness
description: Diagnose a FIFO harness whose proofs are vacuous, triage a real and a spurious counterexample against the interface specification, replay the real one in UVM, and fix the full flag.

steps.title: Step 1: Read the harness and predict
steps.instructions: Open `testbench_buggy.sv` and find `fifo`, `fifo_props` and the `bind`. List each `assume`, `assert` and `cover`, and say whether the interface specification in the README supports each assumption (it promises only: no push while `full`, no pop while `empty`). Predict the formal result for `p_count_in_range`, `p_full_is_correct`, `c_reach_depth` and `c_push_pop`.

steps.title: Step 2: Run as shipped and read the covers first
steps.instructions: Expected: `p_count_in_range` proven; `p_full_is_correct` proven but vacuous; `c_reach_depth` unreachable; `c_push_pop` covered at edge 1. Name the assumption that makes a full FIFO unreachable and explain why the specification does not support it. Explain why `c_push_pop` did not reveal it. Check in the lesson's visualizer: late-flag RTL, contract, `a_never_fill` on.

steps.title: Step 3: Remove the over-constraint and triage the counterexample
steps.instructions: Delete `a_never_fill`. Expected: `p_full_is_correct` counterexample at edge 4 (push at edges 0 to 3; count = 4 and full = 0 at edge 4); `p_count_in_range` counterexample at edge 5; `c_reach_depth` covered at edge 4. Check every environment-driven input in the trace against the specification and decide: design bug or missing assumption? Explain why the fifth push in the second counterexample is legal.

steps.title: Step 4: Write the replay sequence
steps.instructions: In `cex_replay_seq.sv`, fill `push_v` and `pop_v` with the inputs of edges 0 to 3 of the step-3 trace and complete the loop. Assign the item fields rather than calling `randomize()`, and say why. Predict the simulation result: `p_full_is_correct` fails 4 edges after the first replayed push, with count = 4 and full = 0, on a driver that applies one item per clock and idles afterwards.

steps.title: Step 5: Fix the RTL and re-prove
steps.instructions: Fix `full` in `fifo` with a registered flag computed from the next count (`full <= (count_next == DEPTH)`), not with `assign full = (count == DEPTH)`, which would make `p_full_is_correct` restate the RTL. Expected with the contract only: both assertions proven (not vacuous), `c_reach_depth` covered at edge 4, `c_push_pop` covered at edge 1. The replay test now passes.

steps.title: Step 6: Triage a spurious counterexample
steps.instructions: On the fixed RTL, comment out `a_no_push_when_full`. Expected: `p_count_in_range` counterexample at edge 5 (push at edges 0 to 4; count = 4 and full = 1 at edge 4); `p_full_is_correct` proven. Decide whether it is a design bug, explain why replaying it with only the formal run's own assumptions could not tell you, then restore the assumption.
